native_retrieval.snippet: The U.S. House of Representatives narrowly passed its version of a sweeping defense policy bill Wednesday, approving a historic $1.15 trillion budget for the Pentagon amid uncertainty on the future of the Iran war. The bill would have the Department of Defense officially adopt a name change to Department of War. The massive bill also includes a 5% to 7% pay raise for military service members, an increase in active-duty force size and a mandate to revert the names of nine southern military bases to those recommended in 2023 to replace Confederate honorifics. Other lawmakers said the bill’s high price tag would cost American taxpayers too much during a time when citizens are already struggling, and as the country is in the midst of a widely unpopular war in Iran. “Most of that [new deficit] spending is for President Trump’s Iran war, a reckless decision with absolutely no plan on how to achieve victory and how it would end,” House Budget Committee Ranking Member Rep. Brendan Boyle, D-Pa., said during the session.

english_retrieval.title: Protesters in India reject Modi’s promise of fast-track courts for exam leaks - NBC News
english_retrieval.snippet: # Protesters in India reject Modi’s promise of fast-track courts for exam leaks. Opposition groups disrupted parliament for the fourth day this week as protesters from India’s “cockroach” movement continued to demand education reforms. NEW DELHI — Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Thursday that “fast-track” courts would be set up to prosecute those behind exam paper leaks, his first public response after days of youth protests demanding the resignation of the education minister. However, the protesters and opposition parties swiftly rejected Modi’s proposal and insisted that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan quit first, with opposition groups disrupting parliament for the fourth day this week. Opposition parties have echoed the demands of the youth movement and have disrupted the monsoon session of parliament that began this week. “We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks,” he said, adding that those who try to harm the future of young people will not be spared.

english_retrieval.title: Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march - NBC News
english_retrieval.snippet: # Police cane supporters of India’s cockroach movement as thousands gather for march. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office. NEW DELHI — Supporters of India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement were caned by police Monday as they sought to march on parliament in the capital, New Delhi, despite authorities denying permission for the protest. The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office, drawing millions of supporters on social media before broadening its appeal. A police decision to forcibly move hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital on Saturday has galvanized the movement, with thousands of supporters arriving through the night at the protest site of Jantar Mantar in the heart of New Delhi for the march on the opening day of parliament’s monsoon session.

english_retrieval.title: ‘Cockroach’ protests spread across India as leading activist ends hunger strike - NBC News
english_retrieval.snippet: Sonam Wangchuk said he ended his 26-day hunger strike after appeals from lawmakers. An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that helped to galvanize India’s youth-led “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the most sustained challenges to the country’s leadership in years. But demonstrators vowed Friday to press on despite Sonam Wangchuk’s decision to end his fast, as the protests spread from the capital New Dehli to other cities around the country including Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad. Wangchuk’s fastbegan amid protests about education reforms after alleged leaks in some of the country’s most competitive university entrance exams, but quickly became a lightning rod for public anger over education, economic inequality and the rule of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Wangchuk said in a post on X that he ended his fast after appeals from dozens of members of parliament and following “a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country.” Conceding that not all his demands were met, he said two federal lawmakers were present when he finished.
